12:28.note: Jeroboam sets up his calves with Aaron's very formula — 'Behold thy gods, Israel, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt' — the apostasy quoting the apostasy.

evidence.source: the glory of our Lord had filled the house of our Lord
evidence.target: the cloud covered the tabernacle of testimony, and the glory of our Lord filled it

8:11.note: Solomon's dedication replays the tabernacle's: the cloud, and the glory of the Lord filling the house, so the priests cannot stand. (In this corpus Exodus 40 runs to thirty-six verses; the filling of the tabernacle stands at 40:32.)

evidence.source: the fire of our Lord fell, and devoured the holocaust, and the wood, and the stones
evidence.target: a fire coming forth from our Lord, devoured the holocaust, and the fat that was upon the altar

18:38.note: Carmel replays the tabernacle's dedication: fire from the Lord falls and devours the holocaust, and all the people fall on their faces as Israel did at Aaron's first altar. Solomon's dedication repeats it again (2 Paralipomenon 7:1, entered separately).

evidence.source: they brought him forth without the city, and killed him with stones
evidence.target: Bring forth the blasphemer without the camp, and let all that heard him put their hands upon his head, and let all the people stone him

21:13.note: Naboth is condemned on a manufactured blasphemy charge and executed in the blasphemy law's own form — brought forth outside and stoned by the multitude. Stephen's death follows the same shape without the law's warrant (Acts 7:58, set aside: no verbal anchor).

evidence.source: And he said: I saw all Israel dispersed in the mountains, as sheep not having a shepherd, and our Lord said: These have no master
evidence.target: and may go out and enter in before them, and bring them out, or bring them in: lest the people of our Lord be as sheep without a pastor

22:17.note: Micheas' vision over Ahab is Moses' fear for the congregation after him, in the same figure: Israel scattered as sheep not having a shepherd — and the Lord's answer there is that they have no master.

evidence.source: mouth to mouth I speak to him: and plainly, and not by riddles and figures doth he see the Lord
evidence.target: spake unto Moyses face to face, as a man is wont to speak to his friend

12:8.note: God's defence of Moses against Miriam and Aaron rests on Exodus' word: with him he speaks 'mouth to mouth', as at Sinai he spoke 'face to face, as a man is wont to speak to his friend'.

evidence.source: The Lord is patient and full of mercy, taking away iniquity and wicked deeds
evidence.target: merciful and clement, patient and of much compassion

14:18.note: Moses, pleading after the spies, quotes God's own proclamation on Sinai back to him — patient, full of mercy, taking away iniquity; the quotation runs on into 34:7, to the visiting of the fathers' sins upon the children.

evidence.source: For Nadab and Abiu died, when they offered the strange fire in the sight of our Lord
evidence.target: offering before our Lord strange fire, which was not commanded them

3:4.note: The genealogy retells the book's own tragedy in a single clause: strange fire, which was not commanded. The same retelling at Numbers 26:61 is set aside as a duplicate.

evidence.source: let all the multitude stone him without the camp
evidence.target: Bring forth the blasphemer without the camp, and let all that heard him put their hands upon his head, and let all the people stone him

15:35.note: The sentence on the sabbath wood-gatherer is pronounced in the blasphemy law's own form — brought forth without the camp and stoned by all the people — though his offence was the sabbath, not the Name.

evidence.source: a fire also coming forth from our Lord, slew the two hundred fifty men, that offered the incense
evidence.target: And fire coming forth from our Lord, devoured them, & they died before our Lord

16:35.note: Core's company repeats Nadab and Abihu's offence — incense offered without command — and meets their fire. Unauthorized incense is answered from the same presence in both books.

evidence.source: and I will take of thy spirit, and will deliver to them, that they may sustain with thee the burden of the people, and thou only be not burdened
evidence.target: & so it may be lighter for thee, the burden being imparted unto others

11:17.note: The seventy elders are Jethro's counsel come of age: the burden of the people imparted to others — now with Moses' own spirit delivered to them, which Exodus' judges did not have.

evidence.source: because you did offend me in the desert Sin in the contradiction of the multitude, neither would you sanctify me before them upon the waters
evidence.target: Because you have not believed me, to sanctify me before the children of Israel, you shall not bring in these peoples into the land, which I will give them

27:14.note: When Moses must provide his successor, the old sentence is recited once more — the book keeps its own record straight, word for word in the charge.

evidence.source: thou a propitious God, & gracious, and merciful, long suffering and of much compassion, didst not forsake them
evidence.target: merciful and clement, patient and of much compassion

9:17.note: The Levites' great prayer confesses Israel's rebellion in the words of the proclamation: a God 'propitious, gracious and merciful, long suffering and of much compassion', who did not forsake them.

evidence.source: and sinned in thy judgments, which a man should do, and shall live in them
evidence.target: which a man doing, shall live in them

9:29.note: Nehemiah's great confession takes up the life-promise of the statutes, in adapted words, as the very words Israel sinned against. Ezekiel 20:11 quotes the clause word for word (entered as quotation).

evidence.source: that the children of Israel should dwell in tabernacles, on the solemn day, the seventh month
evidence.target: shall dwell in bowers seven days

8:14.note: Nehemiah's generation finds the booths command 'written in the law' and keeps it as it had not been kept since the days of Josue — the feast of Leviticus 23:34-42 revived out of the book itself.

evidence.source: and they hired against them Balaam to curse them: and our God turned the cursing into blessing
evidence.target: That thou shouldst curse mine enemies I called thee: and thou contrary wise blessest them

13:2.note: Read aloud from the law in the restored congregation (the text is Deuteronomy 23), the cursing turned to blessing is anchored here at the moment Balac heard it. The seed points this verse only at Numbers 22 by chapter.

evidence.source: and they possessed the land of Sehon, and the land of the king Hesebon, and the land of Og the king of Basan
evidence.target: Of whom he was strucken in the edge of the sword, and his land was possessed from Arnon unto Jeboc

9:22.note: Nehemias' great confession counts the firstfruits of the promise kept as these two kingdoms east of Jordan — Sehon's land and Og's, possessed in this chapter.

evidence.source: because he is benign & merciful, patient and of much mercy
evidence.target: merciful and clement, patient and of much compassion

2:13.note: Joel summons Israel to return on the strength of the proclamation: 'he is benign and merciful, patient and of much mercy'.

evidence.source: I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh: and your sons, and your daughters shall prophesy
evidence.target: O that all the people might prophesy, and that our Lord would give them his spirit!

2:28.note: What Moses wished over Eldad and Medad — all the people prophesying, the Lord giving them his spirit — Joel promises outright: the spirit poured on all flesh. Peter preaches Joel's form at Pentecost; the wish underneath it is this verse.

evidence.source: I know that thou art a clement, and merciful God, patient, and of much compassion, and forgiving upon the evil
evidence.target: merciful and clement, patient and of much compassion

4:2.note: Jonas quotes the proclamation back at God as a complaint — 'I know that thou art a clement and merciful God, patient and of much compassion' — the formula almost word for word, turned into a grievance that Nineveh was spared.

evidence.source: Our Lord is patient, and great of strength, and cleansing, he will not make innocent
evidence.target: no man of himself is innocent before thee

1:3.note: Nahum takes the proclamation's severe edge: the Lord is patient, but 'cleansing, he will not make innocent' — Exodus: 'no man of himself is innocent before thee'.

evidence.source: God is jealous, & our Lord revenging
evidence.target: The Lord his name is Jealous, God is an emulator

1:2.note: Nahum's God 'is jealous' — Exodus gives the jealousy a name: 'The Lord, his name is Jealous'.

evidence.source: the children of Israel could not behold the face of Moyses for the glory of his countenance
evidence.target: seeing the face of Moyses horned, they were afraid to come near

3:7.note: Paul: the children of Israel 'could not behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance'; Exodus: seeing Moses' face — the DR prints 'horned', for the Vulgate's word — 'they were afraid to come near'.

evidence.source: when he shall be converted to our Lord, the veil shall be taken away
evidence.target: Which going in to our Lord, and speaking with him, he took away until he went forth

3:16.note: Paul reads Moses' own act spiritually: as Moses, going in before the Lord, took away the veil (named at 34:33 and 34:35) until he came forth, so 'when he shall be converted to the Lord, the veil shall be taken away'.

evidence.source: That I will dwell, and walk in them, and will be their God; and they shall be my people
evidence.target: I will walk among you, & will be your God, & you shall be my people

6:16.note: Paul's temple catena quotes the covenant promise of Leviticus 26:11-12. The seed carries this verse of Paul at 26:11 (the tabernacle clause); the walking-and-people clause stands at 26:12.

evidence.source: that no man should consecrate his son or daughter by fire to Moloch
evidence.target: Of thy seed thou shalt not give to be consecrated to the idol Moloch

23:10.note: Josiah defiles Topheth to end the rite Leviticus 18:21 forbids — seed consecrated to Moloch, passed through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom.

evidence.source: We therefore boiled my son, and did eat him
evidence.target: so that you shall eat the flesh of your sons & of your daughters

6:29.note: In the Samaria siege the covenant curse stops being a threat: two mothers boil and eat a son, and the king of Israel hears the case in the famine Leviticus 26:29 foretold. Ezekiel re-pronounces the same curse (entered as allusion).

evidence.source: But the money for offence, & the money for sins, they brought not into the temple of our Lord, because it was the Priests'
evidence.target: the law of both hosts shall be one: to the Priest that offereth it, it shall pertain

12:16.note: Joas's temple repairs respect the old rule: the money for offence and for sins is not treasury income, because Leviticus assigns both hosts — and their price — to the priest who offers them.

evidence.source: For we are pilgrims before thee, and strangers, as all our fathers
evidence.target: you are my strangers & sojourners

29:15.note: David's prayer over the temple treasury takes its self-understanding from the land law: because the land is God's, even Israel's king is his stranger and sojourner, and nothing dedicated is truly his own.

evidence.source: shall put it upon the tip of the right ear of him that is cleansed, and upon the thumbs of his right hand and foot
evidence.target: he had touched the tip of the right ear of every one, and the thumbs of the right hand and foot

14:14.note: Within the book itself: the cleansed leper is restored with the consecration rite of Aaron's sons — the host's blood on the right ear, the right thumb, the right foot — as one re-ordained into the camp.

evidence.source: and with the error of Balaam, have for reward poured out themselves
evidence.target: having the price of divination in their hands

1:11.note: Jude's 'for reward' is this price: the hire of cursing, carried in the messengers' hands, is the error's whole motive.

evidence.source: and have perished in the contradiction of Core
evidence.target: and opening her mouth, devoured them with their tabernacles & all their substance

1:11.note: The perishing Jude names is this: the earth opening her mouth on Core's company in their contradiction of Moses and Aaron.

evidence.source: because thou shalt conceive & bear a son, whose head the razor shall not touch: for he shall be a Nazarite of God, from his infancy, and from his mother's womb
evidence.target: All the time of his separation a razor shall not pass over his head, until the day be expired, that he is consecrated to the Lord

13:5.note: Samson is the law's lifelong Nazarite: the angel lays this chapter's razor rule on him from the womb, and his mother's abstinence (13:4) extends the consecration backward before his birth.

evidence.source: There never came iron upon my head, because I am a Nazarite, that is to say, consecrated to God from my mother's womb: if my head shall be shaven, my strength shall depart from me
evidence.target: a razor shall not pass over his head

16:17.note: Samson's confession to Delila is the vow's own term spoken at its breaking point — no razor on the consecrated head; shorn, he is as other men.

evidence.source: And Haber the Cineite was in time past departed from the rest of the Cineites his brethren of Hobab, the cousin of Moyses
evidence.target: And Moyses said to Hobab the son of Raguel the Madianite, his allied: We march toward the place, which our Lord will give us: come with us, that we may do thee good

4:11.note: The Cineans dwelling in Israel — Haber among them, in the days of the Judges — are there because Hobab took this invitation and did not return to his own country.

evidence.source: Israel therefore sent messengers to Sehon the king of the Amorrheites, who dwelt in Hesebon, & they said to him: Suffer me to pass through thy land unto the river
evidence.target: And Israel sent messengers to Sehon King of the Amorrheites, saying

11:19.note: Jephte's embassy to Ammon argues Israel's title from this embassy — the same messengers, the same request for passage, the same refusal that ended at Jasa.

evidence.source: And you drank wine to the Nazareites: and the Prophets you commanded, saying: prophesy not
evidence.target: they shall abstain from wine, & every thing that can make one drunk

2:12.note: The sin Amos charges on Israel is forcing the consecrated to break the first rule of their consecration — wine, which the Nazarite shall not touch.
